Lesson 1.definition: Witnessed and recorded the fall of Constantinople in 1453.
Captured Constantinople in 1453, destroying the Byzantine Empire.
Renowned for his immense gold wealth and famous pilgrimage to Mecca.
Commanded massive Chinese treasure fleets across the Indian Ocean.
His 1492 voyage to the Americas initiated European global expansion.

Lesson 2.definition: His 1517 protests sparked the Protestant Reformation, dividing Europe.
Issued the 1494 Treaty of Tordesillas dividing the Americas between Spain and Portugal.
Catholic monarch who launched the Spanish Armada against England.
Protestant Queen who authorized privateers and defeated the Spanish Armada.
Catholic monarch whose execution angered Philip II.
Broke away from the Catholic Church in 1534.

Lesson 3.definition: Circumnavigated the globe and heavily raided Spanish treasure ships.
Cousin to Francis Drake and pioneer of the English slave trade.
Organized the first failed English colonization attempt at Roanoke.
Leader of the Powhatan Confederacy who interacted with Jamestown settlers.
Introduced a profitable tobacco strain to Jamestown.
Sent an ambassador to the Mughal Empire.
Sent to the court of the Mughal Emperor in 1615 to secure trading rights.
Wealthy and powerful ruler who permitted early English trade in India.

Lesson 4.definition: Believed in the Divine Right of Kings; executed by Parliament in 1649.
Strict Puritan commander of the New Model Army.
Presided over the trial of King Charles I.
Wealthy merchant, slave trader, and pamphleteer.
Returned to the throne during the Restoration in 1660.

Lesson 5.definition: Led the Jamaican Maroons in a successful guerrilla war against the British.
Formerly enslaved African who published a bestselling autobiography exposing slavery's horrors.
Jamaican sugar plantation overseer whose diary detailed brutal punishments and slave resistance.

Lesson 6.definition: Governed through a constitutional monarchy via Parliament.
Observed the extreme contrasts of wealth and poverty in London in 1750.
Author who reported on rampant crime and poverty in 1751 London.
Famous for his 1751 engraving 'Gin Lane' depicting social decay.
